Subject: Question on backup purge propagation for DR data residency review

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. As part of Acme Health's compliance review we need clear answers on how Redwood's backup retention and deletion interact with:

- Primary record deletions (customer requests under our retention policy)
- Snapshots retained for disaster recovery across regions
- Immutable backups / WORM policies (if any) and expected maximum retention window

Specifically: if Acme requests account-level data deletion, how long can copies remain in backups before they are purged, and is there any manual step required by us to trigger that purge? Also: do deletions in the primary region propagate to cross-region DR snapshots automatically or only after retention expiry?

We'd like these details for our auditor. Appreciated if you can include timelines and any exceptions.

Jordan

Hi Jordan —

Quick answer up front: primary deletions are honored immediately in the active serving layer; backups are on a separate retention lifecycle that can retain snapshots up to the configured DR retention window (default 90 days for hosted accounts). Deletions do not immediately remove historical snapshots; they are cleaned at snapshot expiry unless an accelerated purge is requested.

Hi Jordan / team —

Putting the implementation specifics here so auditors have something concrete. TL;DR: backups are immutable for their retention window, but we support a documented "expedited purge" flow for regulated deletion requests.

How backups are stored:
- Primary active data: deleted immediately from the serving layer when a deletion request is processed.
- Incremental snapshots: written every 6 hours and stored in encrypted object storage with region-tagging.
- Cross-region DR copies: by default asynchronous replication to a designated DR region occurs within 1-3 hours; those copies inherit their own retention clock.

Retention & purge behavior:
- Default retention windows (hosted): 30d (warm snapshots), 90d (DR cold snapshots).
- Immutable meaning: snapshots are write-once for the duration of their retention period; you cannot modify a snapshot in-place.
- Propagation on deletion: a primary deletion marks the record as deleted in indexes immediately. Snapshots containing prior state are not retroactively rewritten; they expire naturally at the snapshot's TTL.
- Expedited purge: for GDPR/HIPAA requests we run an expedited purge that locates snapshot objects referencing the account id and removes them from storage and indices. This process is manual and tracked via an internal ticket; expected completion: 15 business days for most accounts, 30 for large archival sets.

Exceptions and notes:
- If a snapshot is already replicated to an immutable WORM bucket (customer-managed on-prem / marketplace agreement), expedited purge may not be possible without customer cooperation; we'll document and surface that during contract negotiation.
- For Dedicated / Private deployments the retention defaults can be set per-customer and expedited purge SLAs are part of the enterprise contract.

I'm attaching a simple matrix that maps retention windows and purge capability per storage tier.

- Dev

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. To summarize the compliance-facing position you can present to your auditor:

1) Immediate deletion: When Acme issues a data deletion for a customer record, the record is removed from the live index and serving systems immediately (same-day).

2) Backups and snapshots: Historical snapshots that include that record remain until their configured TTL. Default policy for hosted accounts is 90 days for DR archives; shorter windows (30 days) apply for warm snapshots.

3) Cross-region behavior: Replicated DR copies are independent snapshots — they will follow their own TTL and will be removed on expiry. Replication does not create a continuous copy that auto-deletes on primary delete.

4) Expedited purge option: We offer an expedited purge process for regulated deletion requests. It is higher-touch and trackable (we provide an internal ticket id and completion report). Target turnaround: 15 business days from request validation for typical hosted accounts.

5) Contractual exceptions: If Acme requires shorter retention or immediate purge across all replicated copies (including customer-managed buckets), we can include those terms in the Dedicated/Private contract (and will note limitations for third-party immutable storage).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll share the backup retention matrix (attached) and a short one-page statement we can add to the contract appendix that describes the expedited purge SLA.
- Marcus will follow up with pricing / impact if Acme wants to shorten default retention or add expedited purge as a standing service.

Would you like the 1-page appendix drafted for your legal team?
